Germany has expressed interest in partnering with Indian companies to manufacture solar panels and batteries domestically, with the aim of strengthening India's renewable energy supply chain. German Ambassador Jasper Wieck said global energy supply disruptions had highlighted the need to reduce dependence on external sources. The proposal was discussed during the 20th anniversary of the Indo-German Energy Forum in New Delhi. The two countries are also looking to expand cooperation in green hydrogen, industrial capacity and renewable energy technologies. Germany is keen to collaborate with Indian companies to manufacture solar panels and batteries in India, as domestic renewable energy production becomes increasingly important for the country's energy security, German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck said. He highlighted the need to reduce dependence on overseas suppliers and strengthen local manufacturing during an interaction with PTI on the sidelines of the 20th anniversary of the Indo-German Energy Forum (IGEF) in New Delhi. Wieck said disruptions to energy supplies in Europe and Asia, including those affecting shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, had underlined the importance of developing domestic renewable energy capacity. He said producing renewable energy within the country would help India strengthen its energy security and reduce its exposure to disruptions in international supply chains. The ambassador also pointed to the importance of manufacturing the equipment required for the renewable energy sector within India. He said the country needed to ensure that its transition to clean energy did not create a new dependence on imported solar panels and batteries. German companies were ready to work with Indian businesses to establish domestic production capacity for these products. The proposal was discussed during the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit, which was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday. Wieck said the event offered an opportunity for Indian and German companies to explore partnerships and identify opportunities to expand renewable energy manufacturing in India. He also highlighted the participation of a strong German business delegation at the summit. The ambassador linked the proposed manufacturing cooperation with India's Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative, saying that greater domestic production would improve self-reliance, strengthen supply chain resilience and reduce dependence on external sources. He said the next phase of cooperation should focus not only on expanding renewable energy use but also on developing the industries and supply chains needed to support the sector. The need to diversify solar manufacturing has also been highlighted by the International Energy Agency (IEA). According to its findings, China accounts for more than 80% of global manufacturing capacity across the key stages of solar panel production, including polysilicon, ingots, wafers, cells and modules. This concentration has raised concerns about the resilience of global solar supply chains. The Indo-German Energy Forum, established in 2006 by the governments of India and Germany, has served as a platform for cooperation on energy policy. It brings together government agencies, businesses, financial institutions and research organisations to discuss shared priorities. Over the past two decades, its work has covered renewable energy integration into power plants, energy efficiency, battery storage and green hydrogen. Green hydrogen is expected to remain an important area of cooperation between the two countries. India and Germany introduced the Indo-German Green Hydrogen Roadmap in October 2024 during the seventh India-Germany Inter-Governmental Consultations in New Delhi. The roadmap focuses on encouraging private sector investment, supporting green hydrogen production and trade, promoting exports and facilitating the exchange of information on industrial applications and certification standards. Wieck said the next phase of the partnership would involve expanding cooperation in green hydrogen, developing industrial capabilities and establishing future energy value chains. He indicated that the two countries would continue working together to support the development of industries required for the energy transition. Building a domestic renewable energy manufacturing base will require more than investment in production facilities. Access to technology, manufacturing expertise, financing and reliable supply chains will also influence how quickly India can reduce its dependence on imported equipment. The proposed cooperation with Germany brings these requirements into focus. The extent to which discussions between Indian and German businesses translate into manufacturing partnerships and industrial projects will be an important aspect of the countries' energy cooperation in the coming years. artigo.texto: As eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos podem abrir caminho para regras mais rigorosas para as gigantes da inteligência artificial (IA) e as empresas de data centers, mesmo que o presidente Donald Trump, um dos principais defensores do setor, impeça medidas federais de repressão. A resistência também se manifestou nas comunidades locais. Segundo pesquisa da AP, cerca de três quartos dos eleitores americanos se opõem à construção de novos data centers em suas regiões. Além disso, restrições foram aprovadas em 44 das 45 votações locais concluídas analisadas pela Redbud Consulting. De acordo com a AdImpact, campanhas eleitorais gastaram mais de US$ 380 milhões em anúncios televisivos que mencionaram data centers. Os democratas investiram mais de três vezes o valor desembolsado pelos republicanos no tema. Um levantamento do Data Center Watch, projeto da consultoria 10a Labs, mostrou que a maioria dos candidatos eleitos ao Congresso e aos governos estaduais defende regras mais rígidas para o setor. Entre os 34 governadores eleitos em disputas com resultado confirmado pela Associated Press, 32 apoiam regulamentações ou restrições mais severas. Desse total, 12 defendem proibições ou moratórias. A OpenAI anunciou novos compromissos com as comunidades onde desenvolve data centers e pediu aos parlamentares federais, estaduais e locais a criação de regras claras para a construção dessas instalações. Os resultados eleitorais também geraram preocupação em Wall Street. O Nasdaq caiu 11% em relação à máxima histórica, em meio a temores de desaceleração na construção de data centers devido ao aumento dos custos de financiamento. Em relatório, o Morgan Stanley afirmou que os resultados favoráveis aos democratas aumentam as expectativas de restrições ao setor. Segundo o banco, novas regras estaduais podem dividir os Estados Unidos entre regiões que permitem a construção de data centers e outras que proíbem esses empreendimentos. Estadão Conteúdo

artigo.texto: LOWER MERION – Lower Merion Township is about to become the next municipality to consider zoning changes to regulate data centers. At its next building and planning committee meeting, Lower Merion officials are scheduled to discuss including a provision for data centers. In October, the township included a draft zoning amendment on its building and planning committee’s monthly agenda. The committee did not discuss the zoning change, other than noting it would be discussed at the committee’s November meeting. According to township officials, Lower Merion’s zoning code does not currently define or specifically regulate data centers as a distinct land use. “Historically, facilities performing data processing and telecommunication functions were addressed as broader office, institutional, utility, or industrial use categories in the Zoning Code,” according to a staff memo on the proposed changes. “Recent advances in cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and digital infrastructure have resulted in the rapid growth of large-scale data centers that differ substantially from traditional office/technology uses in their building size, electrical demand, cooling requirements, backup power systems, and operational impacts. As a result, an increasing number of municipalities across the Commonwealth are adopting definitions, zoning classifications, and performance standards specifically tailored to data centers and associated development.” In October, Radnor Township introduced an ordinance to regulate data centers, restricting their locations to areas along Matsonford Road and King of Prussia Road. That same month, the Newtown Township Board of Supervisors unanimously passed an ordinance regulating data centers as a conditional use within its Light Industrial district. Under the proposed Lower Merion zoning changes, the township would permit data centers as an industrial use by special exception in its light industrial district. According to information from Lower Merion, the regulations on data centers will include setbacks of at least 1,000 feet from any residential zoning district. The maximum height of a data center and any accessory uses, inclusive of any rooftop appurtenances, shall be limited to 60 feet in height. A minimum of five acres shall be required for any data center with more than 100,000 square feet of gross floor area. The light industrial area where new data centers would be allowed sits along the Schuylkill River adjacent to Interstate 76 near Righters Ferry Road. The area is just under 30 acres. The site includes properties such as the Royal Athena apartments, a hotel, and a fitness center. There’s also a small 1.76-acre site along Righters Ferry Road on the opposite side of Interstate 76.

artigo.texto: Brasil tem janela de 3 anos para garantir espaço em data centers, diz setor Na avaliação do vice-presidente sênior de Desenvolvimento Corporativo e Fusões e Aquisições da Scala Data Centers, a competição é global e envolve um grupo restrito de países capazes de receber grandes investimentos em infraestrutura digital O Brasil tem uma janela de oportunidade de três anos para conseguir se tornar competitivo no mercado internacional de data centers a ponto de bater de frente com grandes players do setor, como os Estados Unidos. A avaliação é do vice-presidente sênior de Desenvolvimento Corporativo e Fusões e Aquisições da Scala Data Centers, Luciano Fialho. Segundo ele, a oportunidade vem da limitação momentânea que passam países como os EUA e os europeus com restrição de crescimento dada a limitação energética para sua expansão. "Há uma janela de oportunidade de três anos. É a fila de conexão nos Estados Unidos e na Europa. Para você conseguir conectar um data center na infraestrutura energética, precisa de cinco a sete anos. Nos próximos três anos, haverá um gap de processamento. Se isso se confirmar, essa demanda precisa ser processada em algum outro lugar. Aí entra a oportunidade do Brasil", declarou à Broadcast, sistema de notícias em tempo real do Grupo Estado. Para isso, afirma, o setor precisa se movimentar "imediatamente" para ter tempo de atrair investimentos estrangeiros e garantir espaço entre mercados já consolidados. Caso contrário, a oportunidade se perde. "Para eu entregar alguma coisa daqui a dois, três anos, tem que começar hoje", frisou. Na avaliação do executivo, a competição é global e envolve um grupo restrito de países capazes de receber grandes investimentos em infraestrutura digital. Segundo ele, caso o Brasil não avance rapidamente na criação de um ambiente competitivo, os recursos podem ser direcionados para outros mercados emergentes que disputam os mesmos projetos, como a Argentina e o Paraguai. Falta urgência nas discussões A defesa do setor é que ainda há falta de um "senso de urgência" entre Executivo, Legislativo e a sociedade civil sobre quais serão os prejuízos do Brasil caso perca a oportunidade. Na lista, estaria o risco da perda de autonomia digital. Para Charles Schramm, gerente executivo da FGV Projetos, que elaborou o estudo "Potenciais Impactos Socioeconômicos da Consolidação do Brasil como Hub Internacional de Infraestrutura Digital na Era da Inteligência Artificial" e constatou que um data center de 100 megawatts (MW) é suficiente para acrescentar ao PIB brasileiro um total de R$ 1,5 bilhão, ainda se faz necessário que haja consciência de "unidade" acerca da pauta de data centers. "Precisa de um senso de urgência. E não pode mais ser de cada parte, nem individual de cada setor. Precisa ser compreendido que a pauta de data centers é essencial a todos e que a fragmentação não é nova nem benéfica", apontou. Dependência externa Fialho afirma que a demora na adoção de medidas para ampliar a competitividade do país pode resultar não apenas na perda de investimentos, mas também no aumento da dependência brasileira de infraestrutura digital instalada no exterior. De acordo com ele, atualmente uma parcela relevante dos dados consumidos no Brasil é armazenada fora do país, principalmente nos Estados Unidos. "O Brasil importa serviços de infraestrutura digital. Se não fizermos essa infraestrutura aqui, outros países vão processar inclusive a demanda brasileira", afirmou. O executivo argumenta que a discussão sobre data centers deve ser encarada como uma questão estratégica, semelhante a de outras infraestruturas críticas, devido à crescente dependência de serviços digitais por setores como finanças, saúde, educação e administração pública. Uma das vantagens brasileiras seria a disponibilidade de energia elétrica, insumo considerado fundamental para a expansão dos data centers em meio ao avanço da inteligência artificial (IA). Enquanto mercados desenvolvidos enfrentam restrições de oferta energética e buscam alternativas para ampliar a geração, o Brasil ainda dispõe de capacidade para receber novos empreendimentos de grande porte. Além dos investimentos diretos citados por Fialho, o gerente da FGV Projetos defende que a consolidação do país como um hub digital pode gerar ganhos adicionais de produtividade, atração de empresas de tecnologia e formação de mão de obra especializada, ampliando os efeitos econômicos para além daqueles estimados no estudo.

artigo.texto: Bess-Henning, St. Francis trick Woodstock on first play en route to lopsided 2nd round 5A win St. Francis receiver Greg Bess-Henning’s junior season hasn’t been an easy one. He fractured his right collarbone during a 7-on-7 game during the summer, then broke it again early in the season. Bess-Henning missed six games before returning to action in Week 8. “Shout out to my doctors that helped me and motivated me to come back,” Bess-Henning said. “With that injury, a lot of kids don’t come back right away. “Football is a dangerous game. (Injuries) just come with being hit.” It didn’t take long for Bess-Henning and the Spartans to hit Woodstock with some razzle-dazzle to match the sparklingly sunny sky on Saturday in Wheaton. On the first play from scrimmage, junior quarterback Jadon Wilson found a wide-open Bess-Henning for a 51-yard touchdown on a flea flicker just 13 seconds into the game. It was the beginning of a virtuoso performance by the Spartans, who scored on their first six possessions en route to beating the seventh-seeded Blue Streaks 42-14 in a Class 5A second-round game. Defending state champion St. Francis (7-5) travels to sixth-seeded Cary-Grove (9-2) in next week’s quarterfinals. “That’s a new play that we just put in,” Bess-Henning said of the flea flicker. “We watched on film how hard their DBs come down on the run and so we wanted to try some new.” The play began with senior running back Tivias Caldwell Jr. taking a handoff from Wilson. Caldwell turned and tossed the ball back to Wilson, who saw Bess-Henning running 15 yards behind the defense. “Once I caught it from Tivias, I seen nobody near Greg, so my eyes did light up,” Wilson said. “I just threw it as far as I could. Greg went to go get it.” Bess-Henning caught the pass in stride and loped into the end zone. “My mind was like, ‘Just don’t drop the ball,’” Bess-Henning said. “It felt good, just always being a friendly target to the quarterback.” The quick strike set the tone, just as St. Francis coach Bob McMillen hoped it would. “We literally worked on it all week,” McMillen said. “Every time we ran offense, that was the first play we ran. “We had a little script that we wanted to do our first 5-6 plays. If that one didn’t work, we had a second one coming after that.” Nearly everything went according to script for the Spartans. Wilson, who completed 17 of 26 passes for 213 yards and two touchdowns, fired a 15-yard scoring strike to Noah Turner to make it 14-0. Then it was Caldwell Jr.’s turn. He capped the next three possessions by scoring on runs of 1, 15 and 6 yards and finished with 137 yards on 17 carries. “Our plan was just to execute,” Caldwell Jr. said. “Come out with the energy, play for each other, play as a family and a brotherhood. “My O-line did very great. The defense did very great. It was just a great game overall.” So great that the game went to a running clock after Noah Wasielewski’s one-yard touchdown run extended the Spartans’ lead to 42-0 with 4:50 left in the third quarter. Woodstock scored twice, including on a 55-yard hook-and-ladder play, against the St. Francis reserves. Bess-Henning finished with four catches for 76 yards. He said he’s worked hard to build on the connection he and Wilson made during the off-season. “It’s definitely a tough injury and Greg’s a tough player,” Wilson said. “So he kept working all summer and all fall and he came back from it.” Perhaps better than ever. “Ever since he came back, Greg’s been a high-impact player for us,” Caldwell Jr. said. “You can tell by his dedication and tenacity that he really wants it. “It’s being shown. Even today — first play, 13 seconds in.” More could be to come. “He’s still trying to get his wind back,” McMillen said. “He’s still trying to get into football shape, but he’s a big player for us and we’ve got to continue to get him ready. “He’s a tough kid and he’s really doing some good things for us.”

artigo.texto: Ativistas invadem canteiro de obras de data center da Microsoft em Amsterdã Protesto faz parte de uma mobilização em 16 países contra rápida expansão da capacidade computacional para inteligência artificial Manifestantes invadiram o canteiro de obras de um data center da Microsoft em Amsterdã nesta sexta-feira (6), no início de dois dias de protestos que fazem parte de uma reação global crescente contra a rápida expansão da capacidade computacional necessária para a inteligência artificial. Grupos ativistas anunciaram ações em 16 países nesta sexta-feira e no sábado, de acordo com a coalizão “Stop Dirty Data Centres”, que está reunindo grupos ambientalistas e campanhas pelos direitos digitais em torno de apelos para suspender as construções em grande escala. Em Amsterdã, mais de 100 ativistas se reuniram no canteiro de obras de um data center de IA da Microsoft, marchando de braços dados antes de invadir o local, subir em guindastes, pendurar balões e dançar enquanto a polícia assistia passivamente. Alguns carregavam cartazes com mensagens como: “Dane-se seu data center”. A Pure Data Centres, proprietária do local, que planeja investir mais de US$ 1 bilhão e conta com o apoio da Oaktree, de propriedade da Brookfield, afirmou estar comprometida com o diálogo com as partes interessadas locais. “Pedimos respeitosamente às pessoas que estão no local que saiam em segurança e dialoguem conosco sobre o projeto e quaisquer preocupações que possam ter”, afirmou a empresa. Outras ações planejadas incluem uma marcha em Dublin, um protesto em frente ao prédio do Parlamento em Varsóvia, na Polônia, e uma manifestação contra outro data center da Microsoft na Dinamarca. A Microsoft afirmou compreender que as pessoas tenham opiniões fortes sobre o projeto e respeitar o direito delas de expressá-las pacificamente, mas não tolera quaisquer ações ilegais. Queda no mercado de ações A resistência está crescendo da Espanha à Índia e nos Estados Unidos, onde as ações do setor de tecnologia impulsionaram o que se tornou o segundo dia consecutivo de perdas acentuadas nos preços das ações nesta sexta-feira, devido à preocupação de que o controle democrata do Congresso norte-americano possa significar uma regulamentação mais rígida, restringindo a expansão da IA. Ativistas afirmam que os data centers sobrecarregam o abastecimento de eletricidade e água, competem com o setor imobiliário e outras empresas por recursos escassos e ameaçam as metas climáticas. Eles também apontam para a perda de empregos e riscos potenciais à segurança pessoal e nacional decorrentes da concentração de poder por parte de empresas privadas e gigantes da tecnologia. As empresas de tecnologia afirmam que os data centers são essenciais para atender à demanda global por inteligência artificial e computação em nuvem, além de fornecerem infraestrutura crítica para empresas, governos e consumidores. A campanha “Stop Dirty Data Centres” afirma que não é contra o progresso nem defende o fechamento dos data centers existentes, mas sustenta que grandes obras devem ser suspensas até que os governos estabeleçam regras mais claras. A Europa está dividida entre sua ambição de alcançar os EUA e a Ásia em IA para impulsionar a produtividade e a necessidade de manter controles e proteções públicas que, em geral, são mais rigorosos. Em entrevista à Reuters na quinta-feira, a chefe de tecnologia da UE, Henna Virkkunen, disse que a Europa precisa de mais data centers para impulsionar o desenvolvimento da IA, embora tenha acrescentado que isso precisa ser feito com cautela. “A IA, é claro, é uma tecnologia extremamente importante e precisamos ter nossa própria capacidade”, disse Virkkunen, destacando os investimentos que estão sendo feitos na capacidade de fabricação de chips, em startups de IA e em um plano para construir Gigafábricas em toda a região. No entanto, ela acrescentou: “É muito importante para os cidadãos poderem confiar que suas contas de energia não vão disparar e que não haverá apagões por causa dos data centers, nem que esses projetos estejam destruindo o meio ambiente.” Um projeto do Google na Finlândia enfrenta uma investigação criminal por causa do desmatamento de terras; a Itália e Portugal estão endurecendo as regulamentações ambientais para data centers; e a Microsoft desistiu de um projeto de data center no Reino Unido que sofreu atrasos na infraestrutura. A Holanda tem cerca de 200 data centers planejados, em construção ou em operação.

artigo.texto: Data centers could have a dedicated place in Illinois Farm Bureau’s policy book as delegates consider adding a new section on the topic at the organization’s Annual Meeting next month. Resolutions Committee members reviewed 24 policy submissions from 13 counties during their Nov. 4 meeting at IFB. The full committee also considered nine recommendations from its subcommittees, including three data center proposals from the Natural Resources Subcommittee. In total, the full committee advanced 15 policy recommendations. Illinois Farm Bureau Vice President Evan Hultine, chair of the Resolutions Committee, said the “day of policy work” was a reminder of this goal of the “Farm Bureau community.” “At the end of the day, the real mission and purpose is to do positive things for farms and agriculture,” he told Rita Frazer of the RFD Radio Network. “Farm Bureau is absolutely a grassroots policy organization, and days like today highlight that.” The Natural Resources Subcommittee, chaired by LaSalle County Farm Bureau President David Isermann, considered 13 policy submittals, with six of them involving data centers. Isermann said data centers continue to create buzz throughout the state, so after the Resolutions Committee tabled a Clinton County proposal on the issue during its July meeting, the subcommittee recognized the need for further discussion. They worked together ahead of the November meeting to draft a proposal that would put the topic in one place in the IFB policy book while incorporating ideas from the Clinton County proposal, AFBF policy and “as many safeguards for farmers as possible.” “We know Illinois is going to have data centers,” Isermann said. “There were a number of things we came up with that we thought needed to be added, and that it all needed to be in one place under one heading.” The subcommittee voted to advance its new data center policy proposal along with two related measures that remove data center language from other sections of the policy book, consolidating the issue into a single location. The full committee later advanced all three proposals. Illinois Farm Bureau policy currently opposes data center development that would reduce electric grid reliability or potentially deplete aquifers local communities rely on, while supporting requirements for proposed facilities to submit a water withdrawal plan. If approved at Annual Meeting, IFB’s new policy on data centers would expand on the previous policies and support the “responsible development of large-scale data centers, server facilities and other similar facilities in rural communities.” The policy also would promote responsible stewardship of local resources and respect for private property rights while recognizing the economic opportunities data centers can bring to rural areas. Additional measures in the proposed policy submission include support for requiring data center developers to pay their fair share for electricity and provide a decommissioning plan and adequate financial assurance to the county to ensure a facility can be removed if abandoned. The policy would also support requiring a comprehensive farmland drainage plan when construction or decommissioning activities could affect surface or subsurface drainage and limiting nondisclosure agreements between developers and public authorities to ensure the public has appropriate access to information. Other provisions address how and where data centers are developed, supporting the use of brownfields, previously developed sites and other non-tillable land over productive farmland, as well as community benefits agreements to address local impacts, including those affecting farmland. Three other data center-related proposals did not advance, including the one on hold from Clinton County. The subcommittee determined the issues those proposals addressed were already covered in the new submission or elsewhere in IFB policy. The subcommittee also advanced a proposal from the Cass-Morgan Farm Bureau addressing water quantity regulations, which was later approved by the full committee. The proposal supports maintaining existing high-capacity well requirements under the Water Use Act of 1983, as well as agricultural exemptions included in the Water Authorities Act. A proposal from Kendall-Grundy County Farm Bureau regarding the reliability of the 811 system to locate underground utilities before excavation will also come before delegates in December. The county noted in its proposal that farmers and landowners rely on the 811 system, but sometimes there are challenges with underground electrical lines that are a part of commercial energy projects. This policy change would support requiring underground electric lines tied to commercial energy generation and storage facilities to be included in the 811 system and physically marked upon request. The full Resolutions Committee also advanced these policy submittals from the Natural Resources, State and Local Government and Agricultural Production and National Issues Subcommittees: - A Sangamon County proposal that was amended by the Natural Resources Subcommittee supporting the use of domestic sources of energy, such as Illinois coal, nuclear and natural gas that provide baseload power to the electrical grid. - A Johnson County proposal supporting adding Chinese Fountain Grass to the list of noxious weeds. - A LaSalle County proposal, amended by the State and Local Government Subcommittee, supporting state legislation that encourages all Illinois public schools to begin their academic year no earlier than the first Monday after the conclusion of the Illinois State Fair in Springfield. - A State and Local Government Subcommittee proposal that supports implementing a less burdensome auditing process for small townships with lower annual revenue. - A Lawrence County proposal that was amended by the Agriculture Production and National Issues Subcommittee supporting domestic development of fertilizer production, storage and

artigo.texto: LITHONIA, Ga. — Longtime South DeKalb environmental and civic organizers brought residents together Saturday, Nov. 7, to question the rapid growth of artificial intelligence data centers and how much say communities should have before these facilities arrive in their neighborhoods. The Nov. 7 “AI Data Center Reveal” at Rockland United Methodist Church was organized by Renee Cail, president of Citizens for a Healthy and Safe Environment (CHASE), and Cheryl Moore-Mathis, president of the Klondike Area Civic Association (KACA). Both have been involved in environmental and land-use issues in South DeKalb for years. CHASE grew out of opposition to industrial development in the area and has been involved in fights over projects including the Metro Green Recycling facility in Stonecrest. KACA has roots going back decades to neighborhood organizing over quarry and industrial activity around the Klondike community. The Nov. 7 gathering brought that history into a newer fight over data centers, an increasingly prominent issue in DeKalb County and across Georgia. The panel included Dr. Yolanda Whyte, an Atlanta pediatrician and environmental-health advocate; Jessica Owens, director of data and mapping for Science for Georgia; and Andrea Young Jones, director of government relations and public policy for Georgia Women’s Action for New Directions (Georgia WAND). A sustained hum Organizers had planned for the panelists to give individual presentations, but audience questions quickly turned the event into a more open discussion. With time running short, the presentations were ultimately skipped as attendees and panelists continued talking through concerns ranging from health and noise to water use, electricity demand, tax incentives and local zoning. At one point, organizers unexpectedly played a sustained mechanical hum through the room as part of the program, asking attendees to consider what it might be like to live near continuous industrial noise. Whyte focused more broadly on potential health effects from pollution associated with large industrial facilities, including emissions from backup generators. She raised concerns about respiratory illness, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and cardiovascular effects in communities already exposed to pollution. Drawing on her work as a pediatrician, Whyte described seeing children who come into her clinic for unrelated issues but show signs of breathing problems during examinations. The discussion repeatedly returned to what communities receive in exchange for hosting large developments. Panelists questioned how many permanent jobs data centers create after construction is finished and whether companies should bear the full cost of the electricity, water and other infrastructure required to support their facilities. Shahnawaz Rafi, a visiting assistant professor in Emory University’s Environmental Sciences Department, pushed the discussion in a different direction. Rafi asked how communities should account for the potential financial benefits of a large development, including whether they could direct additional revenue toward needs such as health care or other public services. That prompted a broader exchange about whether economic benefits could offset environmental or infrastructure impacts and what protections should be built into projects before approval. Jones argued that communities should require companies to account for those costs at the beginning rather than relying on compensation later. Water usage concerns The conversation also touched on water concerns surrounding data center development elsewhere in the country and in Georgia, as well as the electricity needs of some large facilities. Owens focused much of her discussion on the tools residents and local governments have before a project reaches that point. “The biggest power that a municipality has in envisioning your future is zoning,” Owens said. She encouraged residents to follow zoning cases, special-use permit requests and local government meetings rather than waiting until projects are already approved. Owens works for Science for Georgia, a nonprofit science and public-policy advocacy organization that has become active in Georgia’s data center debate. The group has developed a statewide map of data center projects and has advocated for measures including environmental reviews, greater disclosure of resource use, community benefit agreements and requirements for companies to plan for facilities that are eventually abandoned or become obsolete. Science for Georgia has also been involved in DeKalb County’s ongoing discussion over how data centers should be regulated. Earlier this year, commissioners considered having the organization assist with a health and environmental review before the proposal developed into a broader call for an independently selected third-party study. County debates how to regulate data centers The Nov. 7 forum comes as DeKalb continues debating its own approach. The county has a moratorium on accepting applications for new or expanded data centers while officials study potential impacts and consider additional regulations. Two data center-related items are scheduled to return to the DeKalb County Board of Commissioners on Nov. 10, including a proposal requiring an independent health and environmental study before the moratorium can be lifted and another calling for broader definitions and classifications for data centers. The discussion Saturday ranged beyond the physical facilities themselves. Panelists and attendees discussed how companies collect and use personal data, targeted advertising, algorithmic pricing and the growing role of artificial intelligence in workplaces. Jones discussed concerns about algorithms determining compensation for gig workers, while Owens described how collected information can predict consumer behavior. artigo.texto: Cabinet Approves Rs. 145 bn Scheme for 92 GWh Energy Storage 09 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share The Union Cabinet has approved a Rs. 145 bn viability gap funding (VGF) scheme to support the development of 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage capacity by FY31. The initiative is intended to expand storage infrastructure and help India integrate a larger share of renewable energy into its electricity grid. The scheme will support 60 GWh of pumped hydro storage, 30 GWh of battery energy storage systems (BESS) and 2 GWh of alternative storage technologies. The projects are expected to involve total investment of Rs. 976 bn, with government financial support provided between FY27 and FY31. The programme is aimed at improving the financial viability of large-scale storage projects, which can help manage intermittent solar and wind generation and provide round-the-clock electricity. The planned addition represents 170 per cent of India’s existing grid-scale storage capacity and is intended to contribute to the country’s projected requirement of 411 GWh by FY32. The Central Electricity Authority’s National Electricity Plan estimates that India will require 411.4 GWh of energy storage capacity by 2031-32, including 236.22 GWh of BESS and 175.18 GWh of pumped hydro storage. The 92 GWh covered by the new scheme would meet around 22 per cent of the projected requirement. Capacity will be allocated through tariff-based competitive bidding. Public and private sector electricity distribution companies will be eligible for VGF support for battery storage and pumped hydro projects, while alternative storage projects can be implemented by public and private sector entities. Battery projects will also require at least 40 per cent domestic content, supporting local manufacturing and reducing reliance on imported components. The approval builds on earlier government measures. In September 2023, the Cabinet approved Rs. 37.6 bn to develop 4 GWh of battery storage capacity, later expanded to around 13.85 GWh. In June 2025, the Power Ministry extended VGF support to another 30 GWh through Rs. 54 bn from the Power System Development Fund. artigo.texto: Regulamentação do Redata está quase pronta e será debatida quando Lula voltar da Ásia, diz ministra Governo ainda estaria discutindo a inclusão ou não do gás natural entre as fontes de energia que poderão abastecer os data centers beneficiados pelo novo regime O projeto de regulamentação do Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata) está "praticamente finalizado", mas só deverá ser debatido com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva daqui a duas semanas, após a viagem à Ásia. A proposta, aprovada no meio de setembro, estabelece uma política tributária importante para o mercado de tecnologia e de construção de data centers no Brasil. “A gente está praticamente finalizando, mas tivemos que priorizar outros temas com o presidente, inclusive os relacionados à viagem para a COP31", afirmou a ministra-chefe da Casa Civil, Miriam Belchior, à imprensa, nesta sexta-feira (6). "Provavelmente, essa discussão deverá ocorrer na outra semana, não na próxima, já que ele estará fora, quando devemos anunciar a regulamentação.” O decreto que regulamentará a nova lei deve definir critérios e procedimentos de habilitação das empresas no Redata, a lista de equipamentos elegíveis, o método de comprovação das contrapartidas e parâmetros ambientais e de sustentabilidade. O Valor apurou que uma das discussões dentro do governo federal é a inclusão ou não do gás natural entre as fontes de energia que poderão abastecer os data centers beneficiados pelo novo regime. Assim, não há, por enquanto, previsão de quando o decreto será publicado. De acordo com fontes, o Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME) tem uma posição mais favorável à utilização do insumo, enquanto o Ministério da Fazenda tem maior resistência. O texto final aprovado pelo Congresso estabelece que, para usufruir dos benefícios do Redata, os empreendimentos deverão “atender à totalidade da sua demanda de energia elétrica por meio de contratos de suprimento ou autoprodução proveniente de geração a partir de fontes renováveis ou de baixa emissão, na forma de regulamento”. O tema já havia sido alvo de disputa no Congresso, o que contribuiu para travar a votação. A proposta original do governo previa o uso de fontes “limpas ou renováveis”, mas setores pressionaram para que o combustível, apesar de fóssil, pudesse ser enquadrado entre as fontes elegíveis. O Redata também prevê a suspensão dos tributos Imposto sobre Produtos Industrializados (IPI) e Imposto de Importação na compra de componentes eletrônicos, produtos de tecnologia da informação e comunicação destinados a data centers. O impacto fiscal estimado pela Receita Federal é de R$ 5,2 bilhões em 2026, R$ 1 bilhão em 2027 e R$ 1,05 bilhão em 2028, somando R$ 7,25 bilhões em três anos. O Brasil é o quinto maior destino de investimentos em centros de dados no mundo. Este ano, a PwC projeta US$ 11,4 bilhões investidos no setor, um crescimento de 49,3% em relação ao investido em 2025 (US$ 7,6 bilhões), segundo dados da consultoria.

artigo.texto: Technology giant Google will build its first data center in southeast Wyoming, and potentially invest $17 billion in computing centers here. The company confirmed its Equality State data center plans Thursday afternoon, “designed to deliver lasting benefits for Laramie County families and businesses.” “We’re committed to partnering with communities to build data centers the right way,” the company said in a prepared statement. “We will pay for 100% of the power we use, and when we build data centers, we’ll cover the infrastructure needs directly driven by our growth.” It was unclear as of press time Google’s timeframe for building the first facility and how long it might take to complete its $17 billion buildout near Terry Ranch Road in Laramie County. The news comes amid a whirlwind of data center speculation throughout much of the state, including in the Cheyenne area, where the industry is already established, with 10 in operation and more than a dozen on the planning books. The bevy of data centers has provoked a backlash in Wyoming and elsewhere. Prominent politicians, including Secretary of State and soon-to-be Congressman Chuck Gray, have come out in opposition to new AI data centers in Wyoming. A University of Wyoming poll published last week found only 30% of residents here supported allowing the construction of more large data centers for AI technology. Google says it is partnering with natural gas pipeline company Tallgrass Energy, electric utility Black Hills Energy, American Electric Power and data center developer Related Digital for the “long-term” investment plan. The first step is a 702-megawatt facility, powered by fuel-cell technology — converting natural gas into electricity — and a plan to permanently sequester electrical generation emissions deep underground, the company said. Tallgrass is already developing a carbon dioxide sequestration hub in Wyoming, it noted. Regarding water consumption — a major concern among Wyomingites — Google said, “our Wyoming data center will be air-cooled to minimize strain on local water resources.” “This is not speculative. This is happening,” Cheyenne Mayor Patrick Collins told WyoFile. “I’ve been talking to Google, for at least a year now, about looking at Cheyenne to see if we’re a good fit for them and they’re a good fit for us, and I think they have determined we’re a great fit for them.” Tallgrass is already prepping a one-square-mile area for the first phase of the project, he said. “They have spent millions of dollars already, and Google will break ground here soon.” Prior to Thursday’s announcement, Google officials met with “more than 200 residents in Laramie County” to gather feedback to tailor its plans, the company said. Cheyenne City Councilman Larry Wolfe said Google’s announcement feels like a confirmation. “You know, we’re not easily dazzled anymore,” Wolfe told WyoFile. “I will tell you that it’s $10 billion here, $20 billion there. What it’s done is it has made us really cynical about projects that aren’t of that magnitude.”

Elon Musk defende transferência de data centers para o espaço O bilionário Elon Musk defendeu a transferência de data centers para o espaço, onde, segundo ele, os servidores poderiam ser alimentados continuamente por painéis solares sem sobrecarregar as redes elétricas terrestres. Musk afirmou que a expansão da inteligência artificial (IA) em escala de centenas de gigawatts por ano exigirá a busca por fontes de energia fora da Terra. Segundo ele, a capacidade de geração energética do planeta não seria suficiente para atender a essa demanda. Em entrevista ao empresário norte-americano Ron Baron, Musk explicou que o consumo médio de energia dos Estados Unidos supera ligeiramente 500 gigawatts. Assim, acrescentar 200 gigawatts anuais para abastecer servidores de IA exigiria uma expansão de aproximadamente 40% da capacidade de toda a rede elétrica norte-americana a cada ano, algo que ele considera inviável. Como alternativa, o dono da Tesla defendeu a instalação de painéis solares no espaço. De acordo com Musk, os equipamentos poderiam captar energia solar continuamente, sem as limitações impostas pela atmosfera terrestre e pelas variações sazonais. Ele também argumentou que, nessas condições, os painéis poderiam gerar cerca de 30% mais energia do que na Terra e dependeriam de baterias menores, já que não precisariam armazenar eletricidade para atravessar a noite. artigo.texto: CATL Slides With Tech Peers as JPMorgan Trims Targets and Storage Deals Pile Up Published on 11/06/2026 at 14:32 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL shares fell 3.7% on Tuesday, caught in a broad retreat from technology names that swept through Hong Kong and mainland Chinese exchanges. The trigger, according to media reports and Associated Press coverage, was Wall Street's AI-driven selloff, with investors fretting that the outcome of the US midterm elections could usher in tighter rules on artificial intelligence and slow the buildout of data centers. The pullback says little about CATL itself, but the battery maker's own news flow gave investors plenty to weigh — a pair of lowered price targets from JPMorgan, fresh market-share data, and a string of storage agreements stretching from Europe to Australia. JPMorgan Cuts Both Lines The US bank trimmed its target on CATL's A-shares to RMB 300 from RMB 310, and lowered its H-share objective to HKD 420 from HKD 440. Even so, the company's expansion beyond China continues to gather pace. Figures from SNE Research cited in media reports show CATL's battery installations outside its home market reached 143.7 GWh between January and September 2026, a gain of 46.7% year on year. Market share climbed to 33.7% from 28.6%. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Europe: Storage Pacts, No Firm Orders Yet On the European storage front, Octopus Energy announced a memorandum of understanding with CATL and its subsidiary Ampace on Tuesday. The partners will explore smart home storage solutions for European markets, including applications built around sodium-ion batteries. The arrangement is described as open-ended cooperation rather than a binding supply contract. That followed a separate MOU signed on 27 October between CATL and INTILION. Under the plan, the companies intend to deploy CATL energy storage systems totaling 3 GWh over five years, targeting Germany, Switzerland, Austria and other countries. Australia: TENER+ Makes Its Debut CATL's most concrete product push came on 29 October, when it introduced its TENER+ energy storage system at All Energy Australia. The unit carries a capacity of 9 MWh. At the same event, the company signed memoranda with Hitachi Energy, EPEC Group and UNSW Sydney covering the execution of large battery projects and their grid connections in Australia. Demand for large-scale grid storage in the country is growing, according to media reports, giving the agreements a plausible commercial backdrop — provided the partners can turn intent into delivered projects. Employee Ownership Sets a Benchmark Alongside the expansion, CATL is pressing ahead with an employee participation scheme. Reserved shares were priced at RMB 158.42 apiece. The program is a sound instrument as long as it ties participants' interests to durable corporate value, which matters for a company balancing new products and partners against a strained margin. Disappointing quarterly results and tax-related margin pressure have already weighed on sentiment, making execution — not the count of new agreements — the yardstick investors should apply. The Australian deals will earn their worth only if they become economically viable projects, and the employee scheme only if it reinforces that focus on results. artigo.texto: CATL's Expanding Order Book Meets a Harder Question: Who Absorbs the Battery Tax? Published on 11/07/2026 at 01:10 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL shares fell 3.7% on Wednesday, and the day's news flow neatly captured the tension running through the investment case. On one side sits a lengthening list of partnerships and project clearances; on the other, a pair of JPMorgan target cuts that frame the same concern from two angles — the difficulty of passing battery-related tax costs through to automakers and energy-storage integrators. The US bank trimmed its view on both listings. The H-share target came down to HKD420 from HKD440, while the A-share target slipped to RMB300 from RMB310. The "Overweight" rating on the A-shares survived the revision, leaving a more cautious valuation wrapped around a still-positive stance. Media reports attribute the lower sector forecasts to softer assumptions on per-unit profit. Volume Is Not the Problem Operating momentum, by contrast, offers a sturdy counterweight. Figures from SNE Research, reported by The Herald Business on Wednesday, show CATL's battery deployment for electric vehicles outside China reached 143.7 GWh between January and September 2026 — a 46.7% jump on the same period a year earlier. That is a formidable volume base. It only becomes a persuasive earnings argument, though, if CATL can serve the extra business on commercially viable terms. Shipments and unit margins now have to be read together rather than in isolation. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? The same yardstick applies to the storage side, where CATL has been busy assembling alliances. A letter of intent unveiled Wednesday with Octopus Energy and Ampace covers smart home storage in Europe, with the UK, France and Spain as the first markets. Ampace is to develop and manufacture cells, battery management systems and full systems, while Octopus contributes European distribution channels and energy-management services. A second agreement, announced on 27 October, envisages 3 GWh of CATL energy-storage systems across Germany, Switzerland, Austria and further markets over five years, in partnership with INTILION. Add in a strategic product cooperation disclosed Monday with Blue Vector — under which CATL becomes exclusive battery partner for the SKYLA V30 aircraft and will develop a tailored aviation battery — and the growth runway visibly widens. Legal and Regulatory Hurdles Fall Away Project execution took two steps forward at the end of October. On 30 October, authorities in Yichun approved the environmental impact assessment for the Jianxiawo lithium mine, operated by CATL subsidiary Yichun Times New Energy Mining. The same day, Reuters reported that a Hungarian court had dismissed a lawsuit brought by local residents against CATL's Debrecen battery plant, removing a legal obstacle to that project. Both developments favour CATL insofar as they smooth the path to implementation. They also shift attention to what follows a permit or a court ruling: the economic delivery. Sentiment around the sector received its own boost earlier, when Reuters reported a rally in Chinese cleantech stocks as investors bet on stronger US support for clean energy following Democratic gains in Congress. CATL ranked among the winners. Political tailwinds can lift an entire industry, yet whether they translate into profit for any single company still depends on its pricing power with customers — precisely where JPMorgan's note lands. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. The Next Test Is Deal Conversion What matters now is whether memoranda of understanding harden into binding projects. The Octopus Energy and Ampace tie-up offers the clearest template, combining technology, distribution and energy management in a defined European framework; concrete implementation steps would reveal how durable the announced cooperation really is. Cost pass-through remains the counterargument that will not go away. If automakers and storage integrators accept only limited increases, battery suppliers may have to shoulder a larger share themselves, and extra volume would then contribute less to earnings than investors had assumed. New partnerships can cushion that risk only if their commercial terms are attractive enough — and with letters of intent, the benefit hinges on which projects emerge and on what conditions supply is delivered. For investors, the quality of the incremental business is the measure that counts. A more durable recovery looks plausible if CATL can pair rising volumes with steadier per-unit returns. Should cost pressure persist, even an expanding order book would warrant a more guarded valuation. Ad CATL Stock: New Analysis - 7 November Fresh CATL information released. artigo.texto: A ministra da Casa Civil, Miriam Belchior, disse nesta sexta-feira,6/11, que o governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) pretende anunciar, daqui a duas semanas, a regulamentação do Redata (regime de desonerações para o setor de data centers). “Estamos praticamente finalizados com os termos da regulamentação. Tivemos que priorizar com o presidente outros temas, inclusive esse sobre transição energética para a viagem da COP31. Provavelmente, essa discussão deverá se dar com ele na outra semana, não na próxima, quando ele estará fora. Na outra semana, esperamos anunciar a regulamentação”, afirmou a ministra. A fala foi em entrevista coletiva à imprensa no Ministério de Minas e Energia, após reunião do Conselho Nacional de Política Energética (CNPE). Lula participou da reunião, mas foi embora antes da entrevista coletiva dos ministros. Sobre os data centers, durante reunião do Conselho Nacional de Política Energética (CNPE), Lula defendeu que novas estruturas sejam vinculadas à autoprodução de energia. Segundo o presidente da República, os elevados custos e a alta demanda energética desses empreendimentos não devem impactar a rede que atende o consumidor final. “Qual é o país que tem condições de investimento em data center que consome energia para caramba mais do que o Brasil? Exigindo que quem vier investir construa a sua própria energia, porque não vai ser a energia do povo que vai ser utilizada para data center”, declarou. O presidente viaja à Turquia na próxima segunda-feira, 9. Lá, ele participa da COP31. Vai emendar com uma viagem às Filipinas, para ir à cúpula da Asean. A volta a Brasília está prevista para o dia 16 de novembro.

artigo.texto: Denza Z9GT: conheça a perua elétrica de luxo de 1.156 cv em impressões ao volante Denza Z9GT combina três motores elétricos, 1.156 cv e tecnologia de luxo em uma perua que acelera de 0 a 100 km/h em 2,7 segundos. Crédito: Estadão A conquista do Yangwang U9X ao atingir 503,17 km/h na rodovia Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed, em Abu Dhabi, vai muito além de um novo recorde mundial de velocidade. Homologado pelo Guinness World Records e pela FIA como o carro elétrico e de produção mais rápido do mundo, o feito mostra como a engenharia da BYD superou limites técnicos para levar um modelo movido a bateria além da barreira dos 500 km/h. Leia também - Após bater a 450 km/h, hipercarro da BYD consegue quebrar o recorde e ultrapassa os 500 km/h - Brasileiro faz Fiat Uno elétrico com motor BYD e bateria de Porsche — e o final inclui um incêndio - Como o ‘imposto do pecado’ tende a aumentar o preço do carro Para superar a marca anterior de 496,22 km/h, obtida na Alemanha, a divisão de superesportivos da marca combinou altíssima voltagem, rotação extrema e vetorização contínua de torque em um conjunto elétrico revolucionário. Arquitetura de 1.200 V e 3.020 cavalos de potência O ponto central do desempenho do BYD Yangwang U9X é a sua arquitetura elétrica de 1.200 volts. O sistema entrega energia com alta eficiência e reduz o aquecimento mecânico, fator vital para sustentar acelerações extremas por longos períodos. O hipercarro traz quatro motores elétricos — um em cada roda —, que juntos entregam impressionantes 3.020 cavalos de potência (2.220 kW). O número representa mais do que o dobro dos 1.287 cv da versão convencional do U9. Diferente dos motores a combustão, que exigem a elevação das rotações para atingir o pico de força, o conjunto do U9X entrega torque instantâneo. São 342 kgfm de torque imediato, força suficiente para impulsionar o veículo com violência em qualquer faixa de velocidade. Tecnologia de tração e suspensão ativa acima dos 400 km/h Para gerenciar essa força brutal sem perder a estabilidade, a BYD desenvolveu um sistema proprietário de vetorização de torque. A tecnologia ajusta a entrega de potência para cada roda de forma independente mais de 100 vezes por segundo, corrigindo trajetórias e evitando a perda de aderência dos pneus mesmo acima dos 400 km/h. Isso também impede a perda de força e potência em velocidades extremas. A gestão mecânica é apoiada pela suspensão ativa inteligente DiSus-X e por pneus semi-slick GitiSport e.GTR2 PRO, desenvolvidos sob medida para suportar o estresse térmico e a força centrífuga do teste. Motores elétricos chegam a 30 mil rotações por minuto Para alcançar rotações de até 30.000 rpm nos motores, a fabricante chinesa utilizou materiais de classe aeroespacial. O estator traz aço supersilício com apenas 0,1 mm de espessura, enquanto o rotor adota aço-silício de ultra-alta resistência com especificação de 970 MPa. A carcaça dos motores é moldada em alumínio de grau aeroespacial, unindo rigidez estrutural e redução de peso. Além do avanço mecânico, os engenheiros realizaram ajustes finos diretamente na reta de 7 km no deserto de Abu Dhabi. O ângulo da asa traseira foi reconfigurado para ampliar a pressão aerodinâmica (downforce) no eixo traseiro. Ao mesmo tempo, o software da suspensão teve o amortecimento de retorno ajustado para absorver as micro-ondulações do asfalto, garantindo o equilíbrio necessário para ultrapassar os 500 km/h com segurança. Essa soma de inovações colocou o BYD Yangwang U9X no topo do automobilismo mundial, superando os recordes históricos de hipercarros a combustão de marcas lendárias como Bugatti e Koenigsegg. O modelo terá produção ultraexclusiva limitada a apenas 30 unidades no mundo. Carregando ofertas...

artigo.texto: Manifestantes invadem canteiro de obras de data center da Microsoft em Amsterdã Ações isoladas também ocorrem do lado de fora da empresa e por toda a Europa, em protesto contra os dados ambientais e sociais causados pela corrida da IA Ativistas invadiram o canteiro de obras de um data center da Microsoft em construção em Amsterdã, em meio à reação contra os danos sociais e ambientais causados pelo boom da IA que se espalha pela Europa. Manifestantes do Geef Tegengas, um grupo holandês de ação direta, entraram em confronto com a polícia ao invadir um canteiro de obras em Westpoort, Amsterdã, onde alguns membros subiram em um guindaste, acenderam sinalizadores e amarraram balões de hélio aos equipamentos. A ação ocorre em meio à resistência em toda a Europa à rápida expansão da IA e ao alto consumo de energia dos data centers. Nos últimos dois dias, mais de100 grupos se envolveram em uma série de protestos para exigir moratórias na construção de novos data centers. A invasão do centro de dados holandês, onde manifestantes penduraram faixas protestando contra os serviços da Microsoft para as forças armadas israelenses e para o Serviço de Imigração e Alfândega dos EUA (ICE), foi um evento separado da campanha pan-europeia “Stop Dirty Data Centres” (Pare os Centros de Dados Sujos), que tinha como alvo o mesmo local, mas cujos membros afiliados permaneceram fora do perímetro cercado. A polícia declarou em um comunicado à NOS, emissora pública holandesa: “A polícia tentou impedir [a ocupação] e prender os manifestantes, mas não conseguiu e a força foi usada. Um policial ficou levemente ferido durante o protesto.” Manifestantes de ambos os grupos disseram que a polícia usou força e gás lacrimogêneo para dispersar os ativistas que tentavam entrar no canteiro de obras. Organizadores e a mídia local relataram centenas de manifestantes em cada lado da cerca. Protestos menores ocorreram no centro de Bristol, no Reino Unido, em um data center em Berlim, na Alemanha, em frente ao parlamento polonês em Varsóvia e na praça principal de Zagreb, na Croácia. Mais protestos são esperados para sábado. A Stop Dirty Data Centres, uma coalizão de grupos independentes que inclui filiais nacionais do Greenpeace e do Amigos da Terra, afirmou que não coordenou nem promoveu a ação direta que ocorreu na Holanda, mas que era "compreensível" que as comunidades recorressem a uma série de táticas por não conseguir participar de forma significativa na tomada de decisões. "As grandes empresas de tecnologia e o governo estão avançando rapidamente com o desenvolvimento de data centers em larga escala, apesar da significativa preocupação pública com os impactos nas comunidades locais”, disse Owen Espley, coordenador da campanha. “Muitos projetos de data centers são planejados com pouca transparência ou fiscalização, enquanto comunidades em toda a Europa são excluídas das decisões que moldarão seus ambientes locais e seus futuros.” As consequências ecológicas do boom dos centros de dados alarmaram alguns cientistas climáticos, enquanto a crescente frustração com o impacto social da IA – desde contas de energia e perda de empregos até o papel das empresas de tecnologia em minar a democracia – aumentou a indignação pública. Nas eleições de meio de mandato dos EUA desta semana, quase todas as moratórias propostas para centros de dados em votação foram aprovadas. Roos Molenaar, um ativista da Geef Tegengas, disseque a luta contra as grandes empresas de tecnologia era inseparável da luta contra a opressão e o fascismo. "Não aceitaremos que Amsterdã seja usada para a criação de lixo de IA e para facilitar o genocídio", disse Molenaar. "Este centro de dados está consumindo nossa água potável para enriquecer ainda mais os ricos." Um porta-voz da Microsoft disse estar ciente da manifestação e que sua principal preocupação era o bem-estar de todos no local e em seus arredores. "Entendemos que as pessoas têm opiniões fortes sobre o projeto e respeitamos seu direito de expressá-las pacificamente. No entanto, não toleramos quaisquer ações ilegais ou que coloquem a segurança das pessoas em risco." Um porta-voz da Pure Data Centres, proprietária do local, disse respeitar o direito ao protesto pacífico, mas que entrar em uma construção em andamento é inaceitável. “Nossa prioridade imediata é a segurança de todos; pedimos, respeitosamente, que as pessoas que estão no local saiam em segurança e dialoguem conosco sobre o empreendimento e quaisquer preocupações que possam ter”, afirmou um porta-voz da Pure DC. Governos por toda a Europa têm apoiado a construção de data centers voltados para a inteligência artificial, visando aumentar a arrecadação de impostos e acompanhar o ritmo acelerado de expansão da capacidade computacional nos EUA e na China — com alguns tratando a corrida pela IA como uma questão de segurança nacional. No entanto, os data centers tornaram-se um foco de indignação pública, envolvendo temas que vão desde o meio ambiente e a energia até os direitos humanos e a democracia. Na semana passada, uma investigação realizada pelo The Guardian e pela Investigate Europe revelou evidências de condições perigosas para alguns dos trabalhadores envolvidos na construção dessas instalações.

artigo.texto: Cabinet Approves Rs. 145 bn Scheme for Grid-Scale Energy Storage 09 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share The Union Cabinet has approved a Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme with financial support of Rs. 145 bn for developing 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage capacity. The scheme will run from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31 and is intended to support capacity that has yet to be commissioned across India. The proposed capacity will represent 170 per cent of the country’s present grid-scale energy storage capacity and contribute towards the required 411 GWh capacity by 2031-32. The initiative is designed to support larger integration of renewable energy, improve grid stability and enable reliable, affordable and round-the-clock electricity supply. Under the scheme, 60 GWh will be allocated to Hydro Pumped Storage Plant (PSP) projects, 30 GWh to Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and 2 GWh to alternative energy storage technologies. The projects are expected to involve total investment of Rs. 976 bn, with VGF support intended to improve their financial viability and speed up the deployment of large-scale infrastructure. Capacity will be allocated through a tariff-based competitive bidding process. Public and private sector electricity distribution companies will be eligible for support for BESS and Hydro PSP projects, while projects using alternative storage technologies may be implemented by public and private sector entities. The scheme also includes a minimum Domestic Content Requirement of 40 per cent for BESS projects. The requirement is intended to encourage domestic manufacturing, create opportunities for Indian industry and reduce dependence on imported components, alongside existing supply-side incentives for battery manufacturing. The government expects the programme to improve the flexibility and resilience of the electricity system by addressing variations in renewable generation and reducing reliance on conventional generation for balancing power. It is also intended to strengthen energy security, support wider renewable energy utilisation and advance domestic manufacturing capabilities. artigo.texto: [SMM PV Flash] Tata Power Commissions 300 MW Solar Plant in Karnataka, Utility Portfolio Reaches 12 GW Tata Power announced on 5 November that Tata Power Renewable Energy, through wholly owned subsidiary TP Saurya, has commissioned a 300 MW solar project for the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) at Koppal in Karnataka, with the plant now in commercial operation. The project uses solar trackers and TP580HG10NB bifacial modules, is expected to generate about 810 million units of electricity a year and mitigate around 103,820 tonnes of carbon emissions annually. With the commissioning, Tata Power Renewable Energy's utility-scale renewable portfolio has reached 12 GW, comprising about 7.2 GW operational, including 5.8 GW of solar and 1.3 GW of wind, another 4.9 GW at various stages of implementation and 0.7 GWh of battery energy storage. The company also disclosed 60 MWh of battery energy storage in operation across three locations in Mumbai at Mahalaxmi, Saki and Mankhurd, with a 200 MWh deployment across ten locations in the city approved by the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission in April 2025.

artigo.texto: Tamil Nadu Mandates Battery Storage for Solar Projects Above 1 MW 09 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share The Tamil Nadu government has mandated battery storage for every new solar project with a capacity of 1 MW or more under its Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Policy 2026. The policy aims to create 10 GWh of storage capacity by 2029, improve grid stability, support reliable peak-hour supply and increase the use of renewable power. New solar projects must install storage equivalent to at least 10% of their installed capacity, with the systems capable of discharging for four hours. The requirement applies to projects applying on or after the policy notification date and to projects commissioned from April 1, 2027. New substations pooling renewable power must install standalone storage equal to at least 10% of their sanctioned capacity. Existing substations must add storage equivalent to 5% in 2027-28 and a further 5% in 2028-29, as the state currently cannot utilise around 3,000-4,000 MW of solar power during the day. Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation will procure 2,500 MW, or 10,000 MWh, of battery storage in the first phase through competitive bidding. The prices will require approval from the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission, while Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation will act as the nodal agency for implementing the policy. The policy covers standalone storage facilities, systems integrated with solar and wind projects, and installations supporting transmission and distribution networks. Existing solar and wind projects can add storage without further approvals, while eligible projects commissioned during the policy period will receive a 10-year waiver of wheeling and transmission charges if the discharged energy is used within the state. The government has also launched a renewable energy application portal covering solar, wind, hybrid wind-solar and battery storage projects. Developers can register, submit documents, pay fees, complete technical scrutiny, undertake load-flow studies and obtain grid connectivity approvals online, while also tracking applications, correcting deficiencies and downloading approval orders. artigo.texto: CATL Backs Buyback With Aviation and Home-Storage Pacts as Margin Questions Linger Published on 11/08/2026 at 02:50 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL has repurchased roughly 19.6 million A-shares through October 31, spending about RMB 5.4 billion, the company said on November 2. The figure sits well inside the RMB 20 billion to RMB 40 billion envelope authorized under its buyback program. The repurchase disclosure landed alongside a separate filing on the H-shares. UBS Group AG's disclosed long position in the Hong Kong-listed line fell to 4.82%, dropping it below the 5% reporting threshold. According to media reports, the decline stemmed from the return of shares under a securities lending arrangement rather than direct trading on the exchange. Aviation Battery Deal Adds a New Vertical Also on November 2, CATL signed strategic cooperation and product development agreements with Blue Vector. The two sides plan to jointly develop bespoke aviation batteries for the electric aircraft SKYLA V30, with Blue Vector naming CATL its exclusive battery partner. The aviation tie-up is the most unusual of a cluster of announcements that has broadened CATL's storage and transport footprint in recent weeks. On Tuesday, the company signed a memorandum of understanding with Octopus Energy and Ampace covering smart home-storage systems, with European markets as the initial focus. Under the plan, Octopus Energy's software and customer platform would be paired with battery technology from CATL and Ampace. The memorandum sets out a framework for joint exploration rather than a product already on sale. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? A second European storage initiative followed on October 27, when CATL and INTILION signed a memorandum to deploy CATL energy-storage systems totaling 3 GWh over five years. Germany, Switzerland and Austria are among the intended markets, and the agreement extends to additional territories beyond those three. Zeng Points to a Terawatt-Hour Era Chairman and chief executive Robin Zeng said on October 31 that CATL expects shipments of more than 1,000 GWh in 2026, up from 661 GWh the prior year. Zeng framed the forecast as the company's entry into the terawatt-hour era. The order pipeline is not the only variable in play. JPMorgan took a more cautious line a day earlier, cutting its earnings forecasts for Chinese battery makers, according to media reports, citing the difficulty of passing battery tax costs through to customers. The same cost-transfer squeeze was cited in coverage of the sector backdrop against which CATL's shares fell 3.7% on Friday, with the stock among battery names pulling back after an earlier rally in what reports described as a sector-wide retreat. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Melbourne Launch and Australian Alliances Outside Europe, CATL presented its TENER+ battery storage system, rated at 9 MWh, in Melbourne on October 28. It also announced memoranda with Hitachi Energy, EPEC Group and UNSW Sydney covering project delivery, grid connection and qualification. For investors, the buyback provides a concrete tally against a backdrop of announcements that range from signed supply frameworks to early-stage exploration. The UBS position change, tied to securities lending, is a technical adjustment in the H-share register and does not by itself alter the company's share count or the value held by other shareholders. artigo.texto: In early October, Joe Naff noticed a couple of guys with machinery across the street from his Smyth County home, climbing up the hillside. To him, it looked like core drilling to test the soil and stone in the rolling countryside of his neighborhood. What looked like noise testing followed a week later, he said in an interview, and Naff’s suspicions grew. Then, in late October, the town of Marion released a statement announcing a developer was interested in about 200 acres of government-owned property in the area — but council members and town staff wouldn’t say who the developer was or what it wanted to build. “If the council can just tell me that it is not a data center, I will back down,” Naff said during a town meeting Nov. 2. There was no reply from the council members. Concerns about the possibility of a data center are growing for Marion residents and Smyth County neighbors who live by the property, which lies just past the northeastern limits of Marion’s boundaries. The town, which is the county seat and has a population of about 5,500, has owned the land for five years and transferred the property to its economic development authority this past summer. When emailed questions about the developer and possible uses for the property, town manager Andrew Keen directed Cardinal News to the council’s October statement. The statement said Marion has been trying to find a good use for the property, even before it owned the land. The town has courted developers for housing, truck stops, distribution centers and manufacturing, according to the statement, but all attempts have been unsuccessful. Then a developer — unnamed in the statement — expressed interest early in 2026, which is why the town transferred the property to the development authority. “We don’t know if this property will pass environmental muster,” the statement said. “We don’t know if this company will select our site over others available. We don’t know if this developer will choose to pursue the purchase of this property.” The property is in a “due-diligence phase,” according to the statement. “Like other localities, we don’t make announcements based on anything short of certainties,” the statement said. A Cardinal News records request for nondisclosure agreements came up empty — the town attorney, Mark Fenyk, said in an email that neither the town or its development authority have any on file. Only one out of eight town council members, Hunter Atwell, responded to a request for comment. He said by email that Keen had already provided a response, and he confirmed he hadn’t signed an NDA. Since the property is in Smyth County, outside town limits, any kind of request to build a data center will have to go through its planning commission and board of supervisors, County Administrator Shawn Utt said in a video interview. The county passed an ordinance requiring a special exceptions permit for data center developments in September — though some residents have said officials haven’t gone far enough to protect the county’s ample agricultural land from data centers. Some also say the original zoning ordinance didn’t have data center language in the first place, so in their view, creating a special exceptions permit allows them into Smyth County. The county hasn’t received any requests for rezoning or a special exception permit for the property, Utt said. The process would probably take about a month and a half to come to a final vote, he said, between a public hearing and meeting discussions, if not longer. Eye on tax revenue The land could be a positive in terms of economic development and tax revenues, Utt said. Commercial use would be valuable, he said, and the county also has a need for housing. He is hopeful an interested developer means good things for Smyth County. “If it’s a data center — let’s put it this way, the bean counter in me wants the tax revenue,” Utt said. “The land has not been a tax generator for us, even though it’s got the potential. Anything would be great, anything commercialized.” But for Naff, the way Marion has handled the process has been disrespectful of residents who deserve to know what’s going to happen in their region, he said. His front porch looks out over the hills that he believes will become a data center. Should one be built, he and his neighbors are concerned about the toll on their utilities, property values and quality of life, as well as any potential environmental impact. A couple have broken down in tears while speaking to the town council about the issue. Their questions deserve answers, Naff said. He was born and raised in Marion, working in commercial real estate in the region. He moved into his house northeast of town in 2007. At the time, Walmart was considering building on the acreage now owned by the town, and he knew developers would be interested in the area, he said. But this result is not what he wanted, he said. “I don’t want a data center anywhere, but this?” Naff said. “This is not the highest and best use of this property.” He has had an issue with the town owning the land far before a data center came into the conversation, Naff said. The town bought the acreage for about $800,000 across three parcels. Marion did not do its due diligence, in his view, to figure out how much the land was worth or what resources it had to offer before signing the purchase agreement, he said. Now, this is the town’s last-ditch effort to make up for the misuse of public dollars buying the property, he said. “Nothing’s coming to fruition,” Naff said. “So, it’s my opinion that this is the Hail Mary.” ‘It’s just so pretty’ Sally Hash owns 90 acres across the road from the government-owned land. She and her daughters have raised cattle, sheep and goats there for over a decade, mostly as a hobby. She is worried about how a data center could affect her animals, she said by phone, whether through pollution or some other unforeseen issue.
